_comment: AOS Sprint 8 — Account Intelligence Engine. Every table here is a deterministic lookup keyed by demand-intelligence's own five category keys (config/demand-signal-categories.json) so Account Intelligence never re-derives which category a signal belongs to, only what that category implies for a briefing. Edit this file to retune wording/mappings — no code change needed.

categoryToDomainTags._note: Bridges demand-intelligence's category keys to the domainTags vocabulary sales-director/runtime/config/practitioner-bank.json and this engine's own supporting-assets.json already use, so Section 8's asset ranking can reuse that real, existing tag set rather than inventing a second one.

categoryToGovernanceRisks._note: Section 3 — which of the nine canonical governance-risk items are likely relevant per matched category, each with a factual why-template ({organisation} and {categoryLabel} are substituted). A category can imply more than one risk; an organisation matching several categories gets the union, de-duplicated, ordered by the strongest matched category first.

ai_adoption.why: {organisation}'s AI is reported live at scale — live systems need a defined human-in-the-loop point, not just a design-time review.
Day-two operation of a deployed AI system needs its own controls; a successful rollout is exactly when informal, ad hoc handling stops scaling.
An AI system operating at scale is very likely processing personal or customer data as part of normal use.
A live deployment needs ongoing performance/drift monitoring — a one-time launch review is not sufficient once it is in production.

governance_trigger.why: {organisation} is visibly building a formal AI governance function — that function needs a real model-governance framework to be defensible, not just a title or committee.
A newly-announced governance programme will be expected to produce evidence it is operating, not just that it exists.
Standing up a governance function is the moment operational controls either get formalised properly or stay ad hoc under a new label.

funding_trigger.why: Newly-funded AI expansion typically scales faster than informal, founder-level oversight can track.
Growth-stage AI expansion is the point where model governance either gets built in early or becomes expensive to retrofit later.
Scaling AI use after a funding round usually means more systems and more usage to monitor than before.

regulatory_trigger.why: {organisation} has a named external regulatory or compliance obligation on record — readiness needs to be demonstrable, not assumed.
Regulatory obligations are typically evidenced through audit trails, not asserted after the fact.
Most named regulatory obligations (e.g. EU AI Act, DORA) explicitly extend to third-party/vendor AI, not just internally-built systems.
The regulatory frameworks this signal typically maps to (EU AI Act, DORA, data-protection law) usually have a privacy dimension.

failure_trigger.why: {organisation} has a reported AI incident or failure on record — incident management is the immediate, not eventual, need.
A failure event usually surfaces a gap in the model governance that should have caught it beforehand.
Post-incident, {organisation} will very likely need to demonstrate remediation with evidence, to regulators, customers or its own board.
An incident that became public usually means existing monitoring did not catch it early enough.
AI incidents frequently originate in or involve a third-party vendor's model or data, not only internally-built systems.

categoryToStakeholderTitles._note: Section 5 — titles only, never invented names. Ordered by relevance to that category; aggregated across an organisation's matched categories and de-duplicated, strongest matched category first.

categoryDeploymentStage._note: Section 2 — a human-readable deployment-stage label per category, alongside demand_engine.py's own numeric DEPLOYMENT_STAGE_BY_CATEGORY (this is a label layer, not a second scoring scale).

categoryAiMaturityLabel._note: Section 1 'AI maturity level' — one label per organisation, taken from its single strongest matched category (same baseScore-descending priority demand_engine.py's own compute_overall_demand_score() already uses to pick the 'primary' category), never averaged or invented beyond what that category implies.

categoryStrategicObjective._note: Section 2's 'strategic objective of the deployment' and Section 1's 'business priorities' both reuse this same table — never two separate guesses at the same underlying fact.
categoryStrategicObjective.ai_adoption: Operational efficiency and/or improved customer experience through applied AI
categoryStrategicObjective.governance_trigger: Establishing accountable oversight and structure for existing or planned AI use
categoryStrategicObjective.funding_trigger: Scaling AI capability with newly-raised capital
categoryStrategicObjective.regulatory_trigger: Meeting a named external regulatory or audit obligation
categoryStrategicObjective.failure_trigger: Containing and remediating a reported AI-related incident or failure

regionRegulatoryContext._note: Section 1 'regulatory environment' — best-effort, from the region demand-intelligence already infers (organisation-profiles.json's own 'region' field); 'Not specified' is left honest, never guessed at.
regionRegulatoryContext.UAE: CBUAE AI Principles and UAE data-protection law
regionRegulatoryContext.US: State-level AI regulation (e.g. Colorado AI Act) and sector frameworks such as NIST AI RMF
regionRegulatoryContext.UK: UK's principles-based AI regulation (sector regulators) and UK GDPR
regionRegulatoryContext.India: DPDP Act 2023, plus sector-specific RBI/SEBI guidance where applicable
regionRegulatoryContext.Not specified: Not specified — no explicit regulatory jurisdiction identified from public signals

outreachStrategy._note: Section 6 — six-value vocabulary, deterministically derived in account_intelligence_engine.py from the SAME buyingReadinessBand/confidence fields demand_engine.py's own recommend_next_action() already computed (a re-labelling for the relationship-opening question this brief answers, not a second scoring engine). Reason templates below, {band} and {confidence} substituted.

reasons.Wait: Confidence in the underlying signal is low ({confidence}) — no outreach is warranted until a clearer, corroborating signal appears.
reasons.Direct proposal: Buying readiness is Very High, or an incident/failure signal is on record — this organisation is ready for a direct conversation about engaging now.
reasons.Discovery workshop: Buying readiness is High — a structured discovery workshop is a better opening than a cold direct proposal, and warmer than pure content.
reasons.Thought leadership: Buying readiness is Medium with a high-confidence signal — sharing relevant insight content is a credible way to open the door.
reasons.Connection first: Buying readiness is Medium but confidence in the signal is only medium — worth a light relationship-building connection before any content or ask.
reasons.Monitor: Buying readiness is Low — not yet worth any direct outreach; keep watching for a stronger signal.

conversationStarterTemplates._note: Section 7 — professional, non-salesy openers, never a sales pitch. Category-specific templates use {organisation}; generic templates are used to fill out exactly 3 starters when fewer than 3 categories are matched.
ai_adoption: I noticed {organisation}'s recent move to deploy AI at scale — one thing many organisations discover at that stage is that governance needs to catch up faster than expected once usage grows.
governance_trigger: I saw {organisation} is formalising its AI governance function — an interesting governance question at that stage is usually how to make the new structure demonstrably operating, not just announced.
funding_trigger: Congratulations to {organisation} on the recent funding — one thing many newly-funded AI programmes discover is that governance is easier to build in early than to retrofit once scaling starts.
regulatory_trigger: I noticed {organisation}'s work toward its regulatory obligations — an interesting question there is usually how much of that readiness can be evidenced today versus asserted.
failure_trigger: I saw the recent AI-related incident involving {organisation} — one thing many organisations find after an event like that is the root cause sits upstream of the specific system that failed.
generic: One thing many organisations in {organisation}'s position discover is that AI governance questions surface earlier than expected once a system moves from pilot to production.
An interesting governance question worth raising with {organisation} is how oversight responsibility is currently split between technology and risk functions.
I noticed {organisation}'s public activity in this space — worth a conversation on how governance is being approached as it develops.

opportunityScorecard._note: Section 9. estimatedSalesCycleByBand and competitionRisk are Account Intelligence's own honest, modest heuristics (not reused from elsewhere, since nothing else in AOS estimates either of these) — documented here as heuristics, not guarantees.

competitionRiskBySignalCount._note: More public signals on record plausibly means more advisory firms have already noticed the same organisation; a rough proxy, not a market-intelligence claim.
competitionRiskBySignalCount.atOrAboveThreshold: Elevated — multiple public signals on record; other advisory firms may already be circling.
competitionRiskBySignalCount.belowThreshold: Low to moderate — limited public signal volume so far.
